title: Flat affine base change for sections on intersections of quasi-compact opens
statement:
Let $R$ and $T$ be commutative rings with a homomorphism $R\to T$, and suppose $\operatorname{Spec}T\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is flat [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-flat-morphism]. Let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let $Y_T=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and write $g:Y_T\to Y$ for the projection. Let $E\subset |Y|$ be an intersection of a nonempty set-indexed family of quasi-compact opens, and set $E_T=g^{-1}(E)$. Give these subsets their subspace topologies and let $\mathcal O_Y|_E$ and $\mathcal O_{Y_T}|_{E_T}$ mean inverse-image sheaves along their inclusions [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. Then the canonical homomorphism of $T$-algebras
$$\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_Y|_E)\otimes_R T\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ \Gamma(E_T,\mathcal O_{Y_T}|_{E_T}),\qquad c\otimes t\longmapsto g^\sharp(c)\,t$$
is an isomorphism. These canonical maps are natural for isomorphisms of the schemes with their indicated subsets, and commute with iterated flat affine base change and tensor-product associativity.

source.place: Tag 0APJ, lemma-affine-base-change, with the canonical maps in equation-sections-of-intersection; functoriality and iterated compatibility refer to these canonical maps

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-qc-open-flat-section-diagram] to the given family. Its nonempty finite-subset refinement gives directed quasi-compact opens $V_F$ and $W_F=g^{-1}(V_F)$, with both ambient schemes quasi-separated, and compatible canonical isomorphisms $\varphi_F:A_F\otimes_RT\simeq B_F$. Here $A_F=\Gamma(V_F,\mathcal O_Y)$ and $B_F=\Gamma(W_F,\mathcal O_{Y_T})$. Since the refinement includes every singleton, $\bigcap_FV_F=E$; inverse image commutes with intersections, so $\bigcap_FW_F=E_T$.

source.place: Tag 0APJ, lemma-affine-base-change proof; finite refinement and qc-open comparisons

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-sections-intersection-structure-colimit] to the refined families V_F on Y and W_F on the pullback, using the compactness and quasi-separatedness from Step 1. The identity scheme map induces mutually inverse maps on section rings for any two presentations of the same subset: composition and the identity follow from the inverse-image adjunction unit. Naturality with restrictions transfers the representative and eventual-equality clauses to the original families. Thus each source and target section is represented on a finite-intersection stage, and a target representative vanishing on the intersection vanishes after restriction to a further stage.

source.place: Tag 0APJ, lemma-affine-base-change proof; equation-sections-of-intersection on both schemes

proof.text: Use a direct elementwise tensor argument. Every element of C tensor_R T comes from A_F tensor_R T: tensor induction handles zero and pure tensors using the source representatives; a common finite upper bound handles addition. Restriction and the inverse-image adjunction unit identify the comparison of such a representative with sigma_F phi_F. Surjectivity now follows from target representatives and the surjectivity of phi_F. For injectivity, represent a kernel element at F. Eventual equality makes phi_F of that representative zero on W_K. Pass to G containing F and K; restriction functoriality and the stagewise compatibility give phi_G of its restriction zero. Since phi_G is injective, the restricted tensor is zero, and hence so is its image in C tensor_R T. This proves bijectivity without constructing module colimits or invoking tensor preservation of colimits.

source.place: Tag 0APJ, lemma-affine-base-change proof; assembly of the corresponding results on quasi-compact opens

proof.text: For an isomorphism of the schemes carrying the indicated subsets, both sides of the naturality square send $c\otimes t$ to the pullback of $c$ multiplied by the scalar $t$. For $R\to T\xrightarrow{s}S$ a second flat affine base change, both composites, after tensor associativity, send $(c\otimes t)\otimes u$ to the composite pullback of $c$ multiplied by $s(t)u$. Functoriality of the sheaf comorphism identifies the target sections under the canonical iterated fibre-product isomorphism. Equality on pure tensors implies equality of these algebra maps by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property](3), applied twice for the iterated tensor. This proves all asserted compatibilities.
